model_interpretation.claim: Parallelizing the independent per-option loop should improve throughput on large inputs while preserving each option's baseline arithmetic and operation order. Limiting the team to the positive run thread budget and input count avoids excess workers; keeping small counts out of a multi-thread team should reduce launch overhead. These effects remain to be measured.
model_interpretation.transformations: {"files":["src/candidate.cpp"],"retained":["Parallelize the per-option loop with an OpenMP static worksharing loop when count is at least 128 and more than one thread is available.","Bound the OpenMP team size by the positive run threads argument and count; use one thread for nonpositive counts.","Move the binomial scratch array into the loop body so each iteration has private scratch state, retaining the baseline arithmetic and operation order."]}

model_interpretation.claim: Replacing the 2,016 serial backward updates per input element with 64 binomial-weighted terminal contributions should reduce work while preserving the 63-step discounting and the specified 64 terminal exponents. Double-precision weight construction and accumulation may affect rounding, so correctness remains to be checked by the controller.
model_interpretation.transformations: {"files":["src/candidate.cpp"],"retained":["Preserved terminal indices j=0..63 and payoff exponents 2*j-64; no j=64 payoff is introduced.","Replaced the triangular backward updates with the 63-trial binomial-weighted sum using coefficients C(63,j), Pu^j, and (1-Pu)^(63-j).","Applied exactly 63 discount factors and accumulated weighted payoffs in double precision."]}

Préserver les bornes et la convention de terminal de T1, le budget de threads, l’API et l’écriture complète de la sortie. Faire valider puis mesurer le candidat combiné.
